newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks drift sideways, digesting data, budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks drift sideways, digesting data, budget.

text.p: U.S. stocks edged sideways in listless trade on Tuesday, restrained by a softer bond market as it digested various economic data and details of a historic pact between President Clinton and Republicans to balance the federal budget and cut taxes.
The Dow Jones Industrial average pulled off opening lows to trade up two points at 8123.
The Nasdaq composite remained in negative ground, trading down around two points at 1562.
The long bond was down 6/32 at a 6.42 percent yield.

"The market is interest-rate sensitive here," Henry Herrmann, chief investment officer of Waddell & Reed, said. "There are all kinds of numbers coming out this week and people are worried. In part, people are also trying to go through the budget accord.
Bonds lost some early ground after the Labor Department reported the second quarter employment cost index rose 0.8 percent, as forecast.
"The ECI came in line with recent trends, which seemed to be taken as slightly disappointing," Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities, said.
Clinton and the Republicans reached a pact to balance the federal budget for the first time in a generation and cut taxes by $90 billion over the next five years.
